newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp, Lakefront offer fund for blacks.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp, Lakefront offer fund for blacks.

text.p: A KeyCorp unit and Lakefront Capital Investors Inc. said Tuesday they started a mutual fund that targets blacks and "those who believe in the economic benefits of diversity."

Key Asset Management In.c, and Lakefront, a Cleveland-based, black-owned investment advisory firm, said the Victory Lakefront Fund was the first of its kind aimed at blacks. The fund became effective on March 1, a Key spokeswoman said.
Key said the growth fund would emphasise "championing the economic merits of corporate diversity to companies within the fund's investment portfolio."
Key said the fund would not exclude companies based on diversity policies, "but rather takes an active role in promoting the benefits of diversity after investing in a company."

"We have two main goals -- to put together a top-notch, high-performing mutual fund product for all investors and to make corporate management of the companies we invest in aware that shareholders view diversity as a business issue critical to the long-term success in the global marketplace," said Nathaniel Carter, president of Lakefront.

The following companies are included in its portfolio: American Express Co., Texas Instruments Inc., Eastman Kodak Co., Ford Motor Co., Reebok International Ltd, General Electric Co. and Ameritech Corp.

Key manages about $50 billion in assets for individuals, institutions, corporations and government. KeyCorp is one of the largest bank-based managers of proprietary mutual funds, with over $8 billion in assets under management as of Dec. 31.
